I found the issue! There were actually **three places** where floating-point precision errors could occur when converting prices to cents:

1. **`parseEuros` in money.js** (already fixed in my first attempt) - handles standard decimal format
2. **`decimalCommaToCents` in locale.js** (just fixed) - handles European format like "39,95"  
3. **`cellCents` in money.js** (just fixed) - handles spreadsheet imports

I've now added `Math.round()` to all three. All 50 tests pass, and your Gym subscription at 39.95 can now be added successfully.
